For under $50, I'd recommend the 70mai M310 for a simple front-facing dash cam. But if you want front and rear recording, there are a couple of interesting alternatives.

Best dash cams under $50 (November 2026)

1. 70mai M310 Dash Cam

About $40 · Best overall

1296p recording, Wi-Fi app, voice control, compact design. Good everyday choice, but no rear camera.

Tracked at $39.99 on Amazon. 
DashCamTalk

2. N2 2K Dash Cam

$49.00 · Best front + rear

2K front and 1080p rear, supercapacitor, screen, Wi-Fi. Strong specifications for the money, though limited customer reviews.

View at DDPAI

3. Rexing V1 1080p

Sale around $49 · Best basic alternative

1080p recording, 170° viewing angle, wide dynamic range. Less resolution than the 70mai but wider coverage.

View at Walmart

My recommendation

Buy the 70mai M310 if you want straightforward accident recording and easy access to clips from your phone.

Buy the DDPAI N2 if front and rear coverage matters more. Its supercapacitor is also appealing for hot-weather use.

One important catch: many budget dash cams require a separate high-endurance microSD card, typically adding $10–15. Parking recording usually needs a separate hardwire kit too.

One question: Do you want front camera only, or front + rear? That changes which one I'd pick under $50.
